source_text: ὑμῶν πρὸς τὰ ἅγια, ὅσα ἂν ἁγιάζωσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ ἡ ἀκαθαρσία αὐτοῦ ἐπ' αὐτῷ ᾖ, ἐξολοθρευθήσεται ἡ ψυχὴ ἐκείνη ἀπ' ἐμοῦ. Ἐγὼ Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ὑμῶν, καὶ ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος Ἀαρὼν τοῦ ἱερέως, καὶ οὗτος λεπρᾷ ἢ γονοῤῥυεῖ, τῶν ἁγίων οὐκ ἔδεται, ἕως ἂν καθαρισθῇ, καὶ ὁ ἁπτόμενος πάσης ἀκαθαρσίας ψυχῆς, ἢ ἄνθρωπος ᾧ ἂν ἐξέλθῃ ἐξ αὐτοῦ κοίτη σπέρματος, ἢ ὅστις ἂν ἅψηται παντὸς ἑρπετοῦ ἀκαθάρτου, ὃ μιαίνει αὐτὸν, ἢ ἐπ' ἀνθρώπῳ, ἐν ᾧ μιαίνει αὐτὸν κατὰ πᾶσαν ἀκαθαρσίαν αὐτοῦ· ψυχὴ ἥτις ἐὰν ἅψηται αὐτῶν, ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται ἕως ἑσπέρας, οὐκ ἔδεται ἀπὸ τῶν ἁγίων, ἐὰν μὴ λούσηται τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ὕδατι, καὶ δύῃ ὁ ἥλιος, καὶ καθαρὸς ἔσται, καὶ τότε φάγεται τῶν ἁγίων, ὅτι ἄρτος αὐτοῦ ἐστι. Θνησιμαῖον καὶ θηριάλωτον οὐ φάγεται, μὴ μιανθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν αὐτοῖς. Ἐγὼ Κύριος, καὶ φυλάξονται τὰ φυλάγματά μου, ἵνα μὴ λάβωσι δι' αὐτὰ ἁμαρτίαν, καὶ ἀποθάνωσι δι' αὐτὰ, ἐὰν βεβηλώσωσιν αὐτά. Ἐγὼ Κύριος ὁ ἁγιάζων αὐτούς.» Οἱ γὰρ δὴ προσάγοντες τὰ ἱερὰ, φησὶν, ἤτοι τὰ ἁγιαζόμενα παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ, ὅσα ἂν ἀναθεῖεν εἰς θυσίαν τῷ Θεῷ, μὴ βεβηλούντων αὐτοῦ τὸ ὄνομα, προσάγοντες οὐ προηγνισμένοι, καὶ ἀναπόνιπτον ἔχοντες ἔτι τὴν ἀκαθαρσίαν ἣν ἂν συμβαίνει παθεῖν· ἢ ἴστωσαν ὅτι, φησὶ, τὴν ἐσχάτην εὐθὺς ἀποτίσουσι δίκην. Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι Κύριος, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, οὐ θεὸς ψευδώνυμος, εἰς ὃν εἰ καί τις ἁμάρτοι τυχὸν, οὐδὲν ἔσται πλημμελές. Τί γὰρ ἂν καὶ γένοιτο πρὸς ἡμῶν εἰς ξύλον ἢ λίθον, ᾧπερ ἂν ἕποιτο καὶ τὸ εὐθύνεσθαι δεῖν; Οὐκοῦν τοῖς ἄγαν δείμασι προσεπανορθῶν εἰς ἀσφάλειαν τῆς ἀκαθαρσίας, τοὺς τρόπους καθ' οὓς ἂν γένοιτο πρὸς ἡμῶν ἀπαριθμεῖται χρησίμως, ὡς ἂν εἰδεῖεν οἱ λειτουργοὶ τῆς αὐτοῖς ὅτι μάλιστα πρεπούσης ἐπιεικείας τὴν ὁδὸν, καὶ δι' ὧν ἂν εἶεν δεκτοί τε καὶ καθαροὶ, τὴν τῷ νομοθέτῃ θυμαρεστάτην διαστείχοντες ζωήν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Τὸν μὲν οὖν λεπρῶντα καὶ γονοῤῥυῆ, καὶ τῆς ἱερᾶς ἐξίστησι λειτουργίας, καὶ δεῖν γενέσθαι φησὶ τῶν ἁγίων ἀμέτοχον, μέχρις ἂν αὐτῷ τὸ συμβὰν ἀποκρούσαιτο, καὶ ἀπωτάτω γένοιτο τοῦ νοσεῖν. Προσάπτει δὲ τούτοις, ὡς ὁμοφυᾶ νοσοῦντα ἀκαθαρσίαν, τὸν ἁπτόμενον πάσης ἀκαθαρσίας ψυχῆς, ἢ ᾧ ἐὰν ἐξέλθῃ κοίτη σπέρματος, καὶ μέντοι τὸν ἑρπετοῦ θιγγάνοντα, καὶ ἀνδρὸς ἡντιναοῦν ἔχοντος ἐπὶ μολυσμῷ τὴν κατάῤῥησιν· οὐ πάθεσιν, οἶμαι, σωματικοῖς ἐπιτιμῶντος τοῦ νόμου, κατά γε τὸν ἀληθῆ καὶ ἀμωμήτως ἔχοντα σκοπὸν, ἀλλ' ὡς ἐν τύποις ἔτι, τοῖς ἐν αἰσθήσει καὶ σωματικοῖς, τὰ ἐν ψυχαῖς ἀποφαίνοντος. Σύμβολον δὴ οὖν νεκρώσεως μὲν, ἡ λέπρα· δαπανᾷ γὰρ καὶ καταβόσκεται τὴν σάρκα, μεθίστησι δὲ εἰς τὸ παρὰ φύσιν, καὶ ἀλλοιοῖ τοῦ σώματος τὴν ὄψιν. Γονόῤῥοια δὲ, καρπογονίας ἐστὶν ἀπόθεσις, ῥεούσης εἰς τὸ μηδὲν τῆς φύσεως· ὁποῖος ἄν τις ὁρῷτο καὶ ἀνθρώπου νοῦς παρενεχθεὶς εἰς παραφθορὰν καὶ μονονουχὶ δαπανώμενος εἰς ἀκαρπίαν, διά γε τοῦ δύνασθαι συνιέναι μηδὲν τῶν ἀναγ
pass_a_gloss: [every man who comes near from all the seed] of yours to the holy things, whatever the sons of Israel sanctify to the Lord, and his uncleanness is on him, that soul shall be destroyed from me. I am the Lord your God; and a man from the seed of Aaron the priest, and he is leprous or has a flux, shall not eat of the holy things until he is cleansed; and the one touching any uncleanness of a soul, or a man from whom a bed of seed goes out, or whoever touches any unclean creeping thing which defiles him, or upon a man in whom it defiles him according to all his uncleanness: a soul which touches them shall be unclean until evening; he shall not eat from the holy things unless he washes his body with water, and the sun sets, and he shall be clean, and then he shall eat of the holy things, because it is his bread. A carcass and a beast-caught thing he shall not eat, so as not to be defiled by them. I am the Lord; and they shall keep my charges, that they not take sin through them and die through them, if they profane them. I am the Lord who sanctifies them.' For those bringing the sacred things, he says, that is, the things being sanctified by the sons of Israel, whatever they dedicate as sacrifice to God, let them not profane his name, bringing not purified beforehand and still having unwashed the uncleanness which it may happen to suffer; or let them know, he says, that they will at once pay the utmost penalty. For I am the Lord, that is, not a falsely named god, against whom even if one should perhaps sin, there will be no offence. For what could be done by us against wood or stone, on which there would follow the need to be called to account? So, correcting further with very great fears for safety from uncleanness, he usefully counts out the ways according to which it might occur by us, so that the ministers might know the road of the uprightness most fitting to them, and through what they might be acceptable and clean, passing through the life most pleasing to the lawgiver. PALL.: You spoke rightly. CYR.: So the leprous and the one with a flux he both removes from the sacred ministry and says he must become without share of the holy things, until he beats off what befell him and gets very far from being sick. And he attaches to these, as sick with a kindred uncleanness, the one touching any uncleanness of a soul, or from whom a bed of seed goes out, and also the one handling a creeping thing, and a man who has any charge of defilement whatever; the law not rebuking bodily conditions, I think, according to its true and blameless aim, but as still in types, things of sense and bodily, showing the things in souls. A symbol then of deadness is leprosy; for it consumes and feeds down the flesh, and changes it into what is against nature, and alters the look of the body. A flux of seed is a putting away of fruit-bearing, nature flowing into nothing; such would be seen also a man's mind carried aside into corruption and all but consumed into fruitlessness, through being able to understand nothing of the things neces
pass_b_english: Cyril: …to the holy things that the sons of Israel consecrate to the Lord while his uncleanness is on him, that soul shall be cut off from me: I am the Lord your God. And any man of the offspring of Aaron the priest who is a leper or has a discharge shall not eat of the holy things until he is cleansed; and whoever touches any uncleanness of a person, or a man from whom an emission of seed goes out, or whoever touches any unclean creeping thing that defiles him, or a human being by whom he is defiled through any uncleanness of his: the soul that touches them shall be unclean until evening. He shall not eat of the holy things unless he bathes his body in water; and when the sun sets he shall be clean, and then he shall eat of the holy things, for it is his bread. He shall not eat what has died of itself or been torn by beasts, so that he is not defiled by them: I am the Lord. And they shall keep my charges, so that they do not incur sin because of them and die because of them, if they profane them. I am the Lord who sanctifies them’ (Leviticus 22:3–9). For those who bring the sacred offerings, he says, that is, the things consecrated by the sons of Israel, whatever they dedicate to God as sacrifice, must not profane his name by bringing them without first being purified, while the uncleanness they may have contracted is still unwashed; otherwise, he says, let them know that they will at once pay the utmost penalty. For ‘I am the Lord’: that is, not a falsely named god, against whom, even if someone happened to sin, there would be no offence. For what wrong could we do to wood or stone that would make us answerable? So, adding correction to these severe threats as a safeguard against uncleanness, he usefully lists the ways in which we might incur it, so that the ministers might know the way of the uprightness that best befits them, and how they may be acceptable and clean as they walk through the life most pleasing to the Lawgiver.

Cyril: So he removes the leper and the man with a discharge from the sacred ministry, and says that he must have no share in the holy things until he has thrown off what befell him and is wholly free of the sickness. To these he adds, as sick with an uncleanness of the same kind, the man who touches any uncleanness of a person, or from whom an emission of seed goes out, and also the one who touches a creeping thing, or touches a man who has any discharge that defiles. The law does not, I think, rebuke bodily conditions, in its true and faultless aim; rather, still in types that belong to the senses and the body, it shows what happens in souls. Leprosy, then, is a symbol of deadness; for it eats away and devours the flesh, changes it into what is against nature, and alters the appearance of the body. A discharge of seed is a casting away of the power to bear fruit, as nature flows away into nothing. Such, one might see, is a man’s mind too, when it has been led astray into corruption and is all but wasted away into barrenness, through being unable to understand any of the things

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

The quotation is LXX Leviticus 22:3–9, checked clause by clause; it opened in section 7 (Leviticus 22:2–3). 'Any uncleanness of a person' renders πάσης ἀκαθαρσίας ψυχῆς: in the Hebrew and LXX ψυχή here means a dead person (a corpse), but Cyril in section 9 reads the clause as touching those who are sick (the leper and the man with a discharge), so the neutral 'person' is kept rather than 'corpse'. 'For I am the Lord' repeats the refrain of the quoted verses and gets no separate citation. 'Lawgiver' (νομοθέτης) here means God. The section ends inside the word ἀναγ|καίων; section 9 should open '…necessary for salvation'.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (rewritten as a literal English gloss from the Greek in pass_a_gloss): [Lev 22:3 cont.] [σπέρματος] ὑμῶν πρὸς τὰ ἅγια, ὅσα ἂν ἁγιάζωσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ ἡ ἀκαθαρσία αὐτοῦ ἐπ' αὐτῷ, ἐξολοθρευθήσεται ἡ ψυχὴ ἐκείνη ἀπ' ἐμοῦ 'shall be destroyed from me'. [22:4] ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος Ἀαρών ... λεπρᾷ ἢ γονοῤῥυεῖ 'is leprous or has flux', τῶν ἁγίων οὐκ ἔδεται ἕως ἂν καθαρισθῇ; ὁ ἁπτόμενος πάσης ἀκαθαρσίας ψυχῆς 'touching any uncleanness of a soul/person', ἢ ἄνθρωπος ᾧ ἂν ἐξέλθῃ ἐξ αὐτοῦ κοίτη σπέρματος 'emission of seed', [22:5] ἢ ὅστις ἂν ἅψηται παντὸς ἑρπετοῦ ἀκαθάρτου (creeping thing), ὃ μιαίνει αὐτόν, ἢ ἐπ' ἀνθρώπῳ ἐν ᾧ μιαίνει αὐτὸν κατὰ πᾶσαν ἀκαθαρσίαν αὐτοῦ; [22:6] ψυχὴ ἥτις ἐὰν ἅψηται αὐτῶν ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται ἕως ἑσπέρας, οὐκ ἔδεται ἀπὸ τῶν ἁγίων ἐὰν μὴ λούσηται τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ὕδατι, [22:7] καὶ δύῃ ὁ ἥλιος, καὶ καθαρὸς ἔσται, καὶ τότε φάγεται τῶν ἁγίων, ὅτι ἄρτος αὐτοῦ ἐστι. [22:8] θνησιμαῖον (dead of itself) καὶ θηριάλωτον (beast-caught) οὐ φάγεται, μὴ μιανθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν αὐτοῖς. ἐγὼ Κύριος. [22:9] φυλάξονται τὰ φυλάγματά μου 'keep my charges', ἵνα μὴ λάβωσι δι' αὐτὰ ἁμαρτίαν καὶ ἀποθάνωσι ... ἐὰν βεβηλώσωσιν αὐτά. ἐγὼ Κύριος ὁ ἁγιάζων αὐτούς. Gloss: οἱ προσάγοντες τὰ ἱερά 'those bringing the sacred things', i.e., τὰ ἁγιαζόμενα by Israel, what they ἀναθεῖεν εἰς θυσίαν, μὴ βεβηλούντων 'let them not profane' his name, bringing οὐ προηγνισμένοι 'not purified beforehand', ἀναπόνιπτον 'unwashed' ἀκαθαρσίαν; or ἴστωσαν that τὴν ἐσχάτην ... ἀποτίσουσι δίκην 'pay the utmost penalty'. ἐγώ εἰμι Κύριος = οὐ θεὸς ψευδώνυμος 'not a falsely named god', against whom sinning would be no πλημμελές. What could we do εἰς ξύλον ἢ λίθον that τὸ εὐθύνεσθαι 'being called to account' would follow? τοῖς ἄγαν δείμασι προσεπανορθῶν 'further correcting with great fears' εἰς ἀσφάλειαν τῆς ἀκαθαρσίας 'for safety regarding uncleanness', ἀπαριθμεῖται χρησίμως 'usefully enumerates' τοὺς τρόπους, so that οἱ λειτουργοί know τῆς ... πρεπούσης ἐπιεικείας τὴν ὁδόν 'the way of fitting goodness', and how δεκτοί τε καὶ καθαροί, διαστείχοντες 'walking through' τὴν τῷ νομοθέτῃ θυμαρεστάτην ζωήν 'life most pleasing to the lawgiver'. PALL: ὀρθῶς ἔφης. CYR: τὸν λεπρῶντα καὶ γονοῤῥυῆ ἐξίστησι 'removes' from ἱερὰ λειτουργία and τῶν ἁγίων ἀμέτοχον 'without share', μέχρις ἂν ἀποκρούσαιτο 'beat off' τὸ συμβάν, ἀπωτάτω γένοιτο τοῦ νοσεῖν. προσάπτει 'attaches' ὡς ὁμοφυᾶ 'same-natured' νοσοῦντα ἀκαθαρσίαν: τὸν ἁπτόμενον πάσης ἀκαθαρσίας ψυχῆς, ἢ ᾧ ἐξέλθῃ κοίτη σπέρματος, τὸν ἑρπετοῦ θιγγάνοντα 'touching a creeping thing', καὶ ἀνδρὸς ... ἔχοντος ἐπὶ μολυσμῷ τὴν κατάῤῥησιν 'a man having a flux for defilement'; οὐ πάθεσι σωματικοῖς ἐπιτιμῶντος τοῦ νόμου 'the law not rebuking bodily conditions' κατὰ τὸν ἀληθῆ ... σκοπόν, but ὡς ἐν τύποις ... τοῖς ἐν αἰσθήσει καὶ σωματικοῖς τὰ ἐν ψυχαῖς ἀποφαίνοντος 'showing what is in souls'. σύμβολον νεκρώσεως 'symbol of deadness' ἡ λέπρα: δαπανᾷ 'consumes' καὶ καταβόσκεται 'devours' the flesh, μεθίστησι εἰς τὸ παρὰ φύσιν, ἀλλοιοῖ τὴν ὄψιν. γονόῤῥοια = καρπογονίας ἀπόθεσις 'casting off of fruit-bearing', ῥεούσης εἰς τὸ μηδὲν τῆς φύσεως. So ἀνθρώπου νοῦς παρενεχθεὶς εἰς παραφθοράν 'carried aside into corruption', μονονουχὶ δαπανώμενος εἰς ἀκαρπίαν 'all but consumed into barrenness', διὰ τοῦ δύνασθαι συνιέναι μηδὲν τῶν ἀναγ[καίων εἰς σωτηρίαν in 9].

changes: Leviticus 22:8 purpose clause μὴ μιανθῆναι fixed: 'so that he is not defiled by them' (old wording read as a consequence)
agency fix: καθ' οὓς ἂν γένοιτο πρὸς ἡμῶν = 'the ways in which we might incur it', not 'might come upon us'
προσεπανορθῶν (present participle) -> 'adding correction to these severe threats as a safeguard against uncleanness'
θιγγάνοντα made to govern both objects ('or touches a man who has any discharge')
'if we take its true aim' -> 'in its true and faultless aim'; 'what belongs to souls' -> 'what happens in souls'
title no longer a bare citation: 'Uncleanness that keeps a priest from the holy things'
checked: Leviticus 22:3-9 LXX clause by clause; refrain 'I am the Lord' uncited as a repeat
